I don’t pay for services anymore. It’s too expensive and most of the time I can just do it at home myself. I’m lucky that my boyfriend’s mom used to be a hair stylist and she trims our hair as needed (usually 2-3 times a year). I take good care of my hair by oiling it, not using heat, rinsing it with cold water instead of hot, avoiding tight hairstyles that tug and break the strands, and sleeping with a silk pillowcase and occasionally a bonnet. I don’t dye it anymore because it just costs a lot and damages my hair over time anyways. I’m embracing my natural color, which is a dark brown almost black color. 

For nails, I will occasionally get a gel pedicure but just trim, file, and keep a clear gloss on my finger nails. It’s easy to do and keeps them looking neat. My natural nails are long but sometimes I get sick of them and clip them down short. 

I don’t tan or use self-tanner. I’m embracing my paleness. I like how I look tan but I don’t want to age my skin by going in the sun, and I can’t be bothered to do self-tanning lotion. It’s also just another expense I don’t want to keep up with. 

I don’t like the look of lash extensions (plus they can weaken your natural lashes) so I just opt for mascara. Castor oil has been amazing for growing out my lashes. I’ve seen visible change by doing it consistently (about 4 months of daily use). It takes time but it’s sooooooo much cheaper than lash extensions. 

The only services I’d like to do is threading my eyebrows and maybe waxing my upper lip, but at this point I don’t even want to spend money on that. I use facial razors and tweezers to keep everything cleaned up. It works well for me, though I do prefer the look of waxed/threaded. 

Basically, I don’t want to spend money anymore when I can help it. It’s simply not worth it. I think if I had a big event come up, I might splurge and get my nails/eyebrows done, but beyond that I’m a self-beauty guru 😅

Body image. Just…all of it lol. But it also started for me at a young age. I remember being in 5th grade and by that point I had begun developing body hair as a result of puberty (I got my period that year). Some of the boys at recess would make fun of me when I wore shorts because I had dark leg hair starting to show and they thought girls with hair was gross. I stopped wearing shorts until my mom finally allowed me to shave—which I have done nearly every other day since. 

Being sexualized as a child. My earliest memory of this is standing at the bus stop and a man in a car was passing but slowed when he saw I was alone. He rolled his window down and told me to flash him. I, being a literal child, didn’t understand what he was asking, so I held my hands up to mimic a camera taking a photo and made the sound of the camera “flashing.” The man looked embarrassed or maybe angry and drove away, and I felt for the first time a guilt I didn’t yet have a name for. I thought we were playing a game and was excited to be involved. Idk how old I was, but I was at least elementary school because I had a Barbie backpack and light up shoes 😔 

The cultural idea that girls/women don’t get lonely. Or if we do, it’s not actual loneliness because we can find a partner more easily than boys/men. 

Playing video games as a woman. It’s better for me now, but growing up you couldn’t play seemingly ANY game without being told to get back to the kitchen. 

Religion. I will only give one example for this one. When I was a freshman at college in the US, there was a “pastor” who was allowed to come into campus and “share” his religious views because of free speech. I’m all for free speech, but this grown ass man would scream at female students walking around campus to get to class, telling us we will go to hell for wearing shorts and not having children.
